extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, research-integrity professionals, and readers interested in scientific retractions and peer review
extracted.subtask_description: A news/curation roundup about peer review, retractions, research integrity, and related investigations. Links and brief mentions highlight problems, studies, and guidance relevant to evaluating research and scholarly practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use retraction databases and standardize retraction notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Making wider use of available resources, such as the Retraction Watch database, and improving and standardizing the retraction notices may help add another important dimension to research appraisals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult centralized retraction databases when appraising work; improve and standardize the content and format of retraction/correction notices so they can be reliably used in evaluation and meta-research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt more holistic methods of evaluating scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: Sector leaders quizzed in Elsevier survey back shift to more holistic methods of evaluating scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move beyond narrow metrics (e.g., raw publication counts or single indicators) and incorporate multiple qualitative and quantitative inputs when evaluating researchers or research programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize limitations of Journal Impact Factor (JIF) in evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Considering average JIF values, its growth is proportional to the number of publications in the area and to its JIF value, leading to an inhomogeneous boost that preferentially benefits those journals with high JIF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat JIF with caution; avoid overrelying on JIF as a proxy for quality because it can produce biased, self-reinforcing advantages for high-JIF journals and fields with many publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for race and ethnicity in research design and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t overlook race and ethnicity: new guidelines urge change for psychology research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow emerging guidelines to ensure race and ethnicity are appropriately considered, reported, and analyzed in study design and interpretation rather than being omitted or treated superficially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combat inaccurate citation practices in biomedical literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Burden of proof: combating inaccurate citation in biomedical literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify cited claims, correct inaccurate citations, and require stronger standards of evidence for claims propagated by citation to reduce misinformation and citation cascades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate and address plagiarism and fabrication promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples and reports across the roundup note plagiarism, fabricated misconduct allegations, and multiple retractions (e.g., plagiarism prevalent in COVID-19 publications; professor found guilty of misconduct; editors resigning after plagiarism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be vigilant for plagiarism and data fabrication; investigate allegations thoroughly and apply appropriate corrections or retractions. Editorial action (corrections, resignations, retractions) should follow substantiated findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutinize data and methods to detect scientific fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: How to catch a scientific fraud; How a scientific 'breakthrough' fell apart amid allegations of plagiarism and fakery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use detailed examination of figures, underlying data, methods, and provenance (and whistleblower information when available) to detect inconsistencies, manipulations, or fakery in reported results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid valence-loaded scientific jargon in abstracts and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Results show that over the last four decades, abstracts have contained an increasing amount of valence-loaded scientific jargon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer clear, neutral language in abstracts and reporting; reduce marketing-like or emotionally loaded terminology that can mislead readers about the strength or novelty of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use investigative and reporting resources (e.g., whistleblowers, post-publication review) as part of quality control
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusive reports and whistleblower cases are highlighted (e.g., whistleblower fired after raising concerns about journal articles on LinkedIn; exclusive editor plagiarism revelations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage and protect legitimate whistleblowing and post-publication scrutiny as complementary mechanisms to pre-publication peer review for identifying errors, misconduct, or problematic publications.
